name: Ringo Popup Stall Trailer
description: A towable trailer that unfolds into a complete retail stall — awning, display shelves, point-of-sale terminal, security camera. Ringo leases these to vendors who want more presence than a cart but can't afford a permanent storefront. Like all Ringo products, the lease comes with comprehensive surveillance that the vendor agrees to in the fine print nobody reads. The Popup Stalls cluster in markets and street fairs, creating temporary commercial districts that appear and disappear with the lease cycle.
propulsion: None — towed by any vehicle with a hitch
autonomy: Static deployment with autonomous inventory tracking
armament: None. Security camera, silent alarm to Ringo network.
common_usage: Street markets, seasonal retail, food service, community events.
story_hooks: Ringo Popup Stalls are being deployed in a pattern that creates a surveillance net across an entire district — the vendors are unwitting sensors
A Popup Stall vendor discovers the camera in their unit has been active when the stall is closed, watching the street at night
